Framing effects occur when preferences change as a function of some variation in framing.
The availability bias is a rule of thumb, or mental shortcut, that allows people to estimate the probability of an outcome based on how prevalent or familiar that outcome appears in their lives.
Recency bias is a cognitive predisposition that causes people to more prominently recall and emphasize recent events and observations than those that occurred in the near or distant past.

frontmatter_snapshot.summary: The information-processing family of cognitive biases — anchoring & adjustment, mental accounting, framing, availability, self-attribution, recency — in which the mechanics of perceiving, coding, and recalling information distort an otherwise-held belief.
frontmatter_snapshot.title: Information-Processing Biases
